title: (No AI) I don’t miss the camera on the Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses

![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/rayban_meta_audio_12.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The other day I whizzed past several people while running in the park, my playlist blasting at full volume. The next morning, I smiled at a barista while ordering a caramel apple-flavored matcha latte. Afterward, I sat on a park bench reading a book, called up a pal to chat about her recent trip to Prague, and then asked my Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses what meetings were coming up on my calendar. The chipper AI voice said I hadn't connected my Google Calendar yet (I had) and asked if I would like help connecting. I sighed and then asked it to play an upbeat song. It picked Kendrick Lamar's "Not Like Us."

title: (No AI) Facebook will let you customize your feed algorithm using AI
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![A screenshot of Meta’s Your Algorithm feature in a menu on Facebook](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/meta-your-algorithm-facebook.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Facebook's new ["Your Algorithm" feature](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/10/introducing-your-algorithm-facebook/) will let you directly add and manage topics you want to see in your feed and Facebook Reels. Meta says your recommendations "respond right away" after you make updates using the new feature by hitting "interested" or "not interested" for different topics. Your Algorithm previously [launched on Instagram](https://www.theverge.com/tech/947898/meta-instagram-your-algorithm-main-feed-tell) earlier this year, and Meta also launched a similar ["Dear Algo"](https://www.theverge.com/tech/876610/meta-threads-dear-algo-algorithm) feature on Threads.

Facebook users will be able to access Your Algorithm or select "interested" or "not interested" from the three dots menu on individual posts. The "interested" and "not interested" buttons may also appear under posts, an …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1010344/meta-facebook-your-algorithm-ai)
